colours._how_to_read: hex = rendered sRGB in a plain patch, median of the 10-90% luminance band. hex_white_balanced applies per-channel linear gains that make the white interior door leaves neutral (R x0.882, G x1.000, B x1.187; reference #a99583, the mean of door J in p02 and door I in p03, both in shade). The hallway set is graded warmer than the bedroom and toilet sets, so materials shared with other rooms (walnut, greige, door white, floor tiles) should share one base colour rather than copy each room's rendered hex.

notes: CEILING: the hallway render model has a 2.544 m ceiling (joint fit; p02 alone 2.537, p04 alone 2.550), 14 cm above the owner's 2.40 m (bedroom 2.539, work room 2.608, bathroom 2.412, toilet 2.344). Heights in this file are in the render-model scale. To adopt 2.40: keep absolute heights for things with real sizes (door casings 2.14, handles, console, bench, drawers, mirror 0.82-2.15) and re-anchor the ceiling-hung items (wardrobe top panel and walnut niche panel to the ceiling, hooks, LED profiles, the bulkhead underside 2.11 if the opening keeps a drop), or scale every y by 2.40/2.544 = 0.943. With absolute heights the hooks (2.16-2.27) must move down.

Cameras: p02-p05 share f = 2013 px (hfov 64.9, vfov 51.0 deg; the bedroom set used 2026 px); p01 (1260 x 840) has f = 876 px, the same vertical field of view on a 3:2 frame. Edge rms 1.25-1.51 px per camera. Free per-camera focal lengths would give 1767 (p02), 1938 (p03), 2034 (p04), 2024 (p05) with almost the same rms; p02 looks straight at a flat wall and is the weakest. Pitch -1.2 to -3.4 deg, roll under 0.1 deg. p01, p02 and p04 are outside the hallway and p05 stands in the dining/kitchen area; use near_clip_m.

Excluded from the camera fit as plan-vs-render mismatches: in p02 door I's near casing edge sits about 3 cm closer to the camera than the plan's z 2.924 (it alone pulls the shared focal length to 1990 px); in p01 door J is seen at a grazing angle with its reveal visible, so its casing edges were ambiguous (the projected plan door lands within about 5 px of the visible edges).

Front door: casing x 0.036-1.054 on the top wall of the narrow part (the plan only marks the handle near x 0.87; the lock and lever measure x 0.75-0.95), casing top 2.142 like the interior doors, leaf about 0.92 x 2.10 m, hinges on the left (x 0.04) next to door I. Opening direction and leaf thickness are not visible.

Plan items: p1-F ('radiator?' on the niche back wall) is the hook row; p1-G and p1-H (43 cm 'door?' on both faces of the hallway/dining wall end) are not openings (wardrobe side panel on one side, plaster wall on the other).

The hallway floor tiles are 45 x 45 cm in all renders (grid from x 0 and from the bottom wall), not the 61 cm hatch of the plan raster. The tiles stop at x 3.63; the living room and the corridor have dark wood-look planks.

Uncertain: the bulkhead over the living-room opening (underside 2.07-2.13, depth into the living room 0.2-0.25 from p01 only); the bench depth (front face z 1.79-1.85); the walnut-panel stand-off on the dining side; door swing directions; the corridor beyond z 4.6 (doors N, O, P and the LED path are not visible in these renders).
Colours are rendered pixel values; see colours._how_to_read.
